name: Kalam: one match, turn by turn
description: Claim ONE queued row on this runner's engine digest and play it: observe, one `model_infer` fanned out over the seats asked this turn (`infer`'s for_each), step, until the engine stops returning views. A failed or late inference is a strike: the seat plays no action that turn, and past the row's strike ceiling it forfeits. A seat whose model declares an output named `memory` or `ant_memory` is handed that output of its last answered call back on its next view, under the same key: absent on turn 0, kept through a struck turn, never shared between seats, and gone with the match. A model that declares neither plays exactly as before. The row is finished in place through Soma's runner gate (/v1/runner/*), with its replay under a key naming the attempt and the last frame, decoded by the engine, in the finish body; every gate statement is fenced on the claim token, so a stale attempt updates nothing. It reads no rating and writes no rating: the runner holds no database credential at all. On SIGTERM Orion stops claiming and lets the match in hand finish inside cron.shutdown_timeout_secs.

Soft, a failed presign ran `put` with a null url, which is a PUT of the whole envelope at the connector root that fails anyway, later and for the wrong reason.

tasks.description: The loop's max is a bound, not the terminator: without this the finishing sweep is followed by every remaining sweep up to max with each group skipped, and stopped_at_turn ends as max minus one. A rejected filter halts the run, which is how every loop here ends; a halt is a normal completion.
